title: T811-902SD ADVANCED IN-SITU DATA PROCESSING FOR SPACE DEBRIS MODEL VALIDATION (EXPRO+)
description: The knowledge on the small space debris population is still limited. Large debris populations are welldocumented,with ground radarand telescopes cataloguing objects >10 cm in Low Earth Orbit and 30-40 cmin Geostationary Orbit. Debris in the cm to sub-cm range remains largely uncharted, relying on statisticalsampling via remote sensing, in-situ detectors and retrieved space-exposed hardware. Due to their highvelocities, small debris impacts are a threat to sensitive spacecraft equipment (panels, de-orbitingmechanisms,exposed payloads) and human life. Space debris models, used for risk assessment, rely oncollected samples to model small debris.Several recent space missions carried detectors, with data being collected more often than before. However,there is still no unifiedway to neither collect nor process these efficiently for the output quantities (flux, objectmass/diameter, velocity, source) to beincluded in a model. With the advances in technology and big datahandling, acquisition, storing and efficient processing becomes more realistic.This activity aims to develop a software that can ingest, store and process in-situ measurements of spacedebris. Itwill produce quantities that can be ingested without modifications in the validation toolchain of a spacedebris model. The measurements should include in-situ impact datasets, focusing on the widely usedpiezoelectric and plasma detectors. The inclusion of in-situoptical data and data from photographic surveyswill be considered. A standardised format, compatible with the needs of space debris models, will be ensured.The development of a conversion tool will be part of the main retrieval and processing software or shall resultin a stand-alone tool that can handle the output of the main software.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SMEs  RD  Entities. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: S3-SW-09 D3S END-TO-END SIMULATOR AND CONSTELLATION DESIGN
description: This activity aims to provide a key enabling tool to support the design and implementation planning of ESA's Distributed Space Weather Sensor System (D3S). The first part of the activity focuses on the development of a generic end-to-end mission simulator capableof assessing the performance of distributed space weather sensing architectures. The second part leverages the developed simulator to investigate and optimise the design of a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellation for space weather monitoring. Finally, the activity will assess and trade off different implementation options for the proposed constellation, including alternative payload configurations, dedicated satellites, and hosted payload opportunities

title: ULTRACOMPACT 778 NM RUBIDIUM SECONDARY OPTICAL FREQUENCY STANDARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop an ultracompact, secondary, optical frequency reference based on a two-photon transition in Rb vapour at 778nm.Description:Ultra-stable miniature atomic clocks are being considered for space applications. The Rubidium two-photon transition secondary frequency standard has demonstrated interesting performance metrics with a further potential for ultra-low size, weight and power (SWaP) integration.Currently, such an approach is hindered by the lack of miniaturized laser sources with suitable power levels and spectral properties as well as a compact physics package design taking advantage of the full capabilities of the integrated photonics and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gas cell technology platforms.This activity aims at exploiting these enabling technologies and developing a further concept of a compact high-performance atomic physics package for an ultra-compact secondary optical frequency standard. The goal of this activity is to provide a fractional frequency stability < 10 - 12 at 1 second integration time implemented using integrated photonic techniques.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Evaluate sources of integrated photonic laser systems delivering the wavelengths and the required spectral properties for the defined system approach. Develop Rb cell techniques and technologies targeting an ultracompact 778 nm rubidium secondary optical frequency standard using chip-scale photonic integration. Demonstrate the fractional stability performance achievable using the chosen chip-scale photonic approach. Evaluate chip-scale optical frequency combs with SiN Kerr comb techniques to provide an initial stabilized direct optical-RF link. Provide a packaging solution to maintain the preliminary performance achieved.NOTE: This activityis currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The finallist of participating states will be known at tender issue.
